https://www.politico.eu/article/italy-hi.text: Italian authorities fined Facebook’s parent company Meta €805 million for using photos and videos from Android phones without users' specific consent, the Italian Data Protection Authority said in a statement Saturday. The fine concerned the "camera roll suggestions when browsing Facebook" feature, which suggests photos and videos from a phone's gallery for users to add to posts. The feature violates the Italian law implementing the EU's ePrivacy directive, the authority said. It is by far the largest fine ever imposed by the Italian regulator. Advertisement Advertisement The investigation, launched in 2025, established that access to a user's camera roll is requested with a single permission for the entire app, which the authority said covers multiple features with different needs. The authorization request was preceded by a generic warning that didn't allow users to understand that they were authorizing picture and video suggestions, the authority said. "If granted in full, this type of permission allows the app to read the device's entire photo archive, usually permanently, without the user or the authorities being able to verify which information is actually being used,” the statement reads. The authority also said it "rejected the objection of lack of jurisdiction raised by the company in favor of the Irish authority, because the ePrivacy regulation does not provide for the 'one-stop-shop' mechanism." Meta has 60 days to get consent separately and specifically for the feature, clearly explain what it does and how it can be disabled, the authority said. It also must be disabled by default, including for those who have already authorized it. Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. It has the right to appeal the decision.

http://www.bgnes.com/european-union/roma.text: Moldova's European integration is a shared priority and a strategic investment in the stability of the region and the entire continent, Romanian President Nicusor Dan said following the European Political Community summit in Dublin, Agerpres reported. Dan called for stronger European cooperation on defense, countering hybrid threats and supporting Ukraine in achieving a just and lasting peace. He stressed the need to strengthen NATO's eastern flank, including the Black Sea region. At a meeting of the Moldova Support Group, Dan reaffirmed Romania's unwavering commitment to Moldova's security, resilience and EU integration. Discussions focused on advancing Moldova's accession negotiations, strengthening democratic institutions and countering Russian interference. Moldova aims to complete EU accession negotiations by 2028 and become a full member by 2030. The European Commission has acknowledged progress in reforms while urging further efforts in judicial reform, public administration and fighting corruption. In Dublin, Dan also met German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to discuss European defense cooperation, Moldova's EU aspirations and the EU's future budget. The Romanian president emphasized that supporting Moldova and Ukraine is essential not only for regional stability but also for the long-term security of Europe. | BGNES
